prompts: Use case: precise-object-edit. Convert the input photograph into an accurately registered binary object-selection mask. Output ONLY a black-and-white mask, same portrait aspect ratio and same framing as input. Paint the entire wicker picnic basket (body, lid and arched handle), plus its immediate contact shadow, SOLID WHITE (#FFFFFF). Everything else MUST be SOLID BLACK (#000000): all yellow flowers, stems, hills, fence, trees and sky. Preserve the exact position, size, silhouette and perspective of the basket in the input. The hole beneath the basket handle must remain black. No photo texture, grey shading, outlines, labels, borders, text or other white objects. This is a compositing mask: white selects the basket edit only, black preserves the original photograph.

Use case: precise-object-edit. Create ONLY a precisely registered binary object-selection mask from this input photo. Same portrait framing and aspect ratio. The entire RED BICYCLE in the right foreground is SOLID WHITE, including both tyres, spokes, frame, handlebars, seat, pedals, rack and contact shadow. Trace it in exactly its input position and size. Gaps between spokes, wheels, frame and handlebars stay BLACK so the background is preserved. ALL other pixels are SOLID BLACK: the wicker basket, yellow flowers, fence, hills, trees, clouds, sky. No photographic texture, grey, text, borders or outlines. White means select bicycle; black means preserve original image.

Use case: precise-object-edit. Create ONLY a precisely registered binary removal mask from this input photo. Same portrait framing and aspect ratio. Select ONLY the wicker picnic basket in the lower-left foreground and its immediate contact shadow: paint its entire body, lid and arched handle SOLID WHITE in exactly the same input position and size, with a small safety margin of about 3 pixels to remove edge remnants. Leave the open hole inside the handle BLACK. ALL other pixels must be SOLID BLACK, including the entire red bicycle, all flowers outside the basket footprint, sky, fence, hills and trees. No photographic texture, grey, text, borders or outlines. This mask will remove the basket by replacing that area with flowers from the next edited photo.

Use case: precise-object-edit. Output ONLY a black-and-white binary object mask accurately registered to the input photograph. Keep exactly the same framing and portrait aspect ratio. Paint WHITE only the red-and-blue kite in the upper-left sky, its complete thin ribbon tail and entire faint string leading down toward the field. Follow their input coordinates exactly: kite approximately x288..356 and y175..253 in a 1086x1448 photo; tail continues to x235,y316; fine string descends diagonally to around x525,y683. Everything else SOLID BLACK, including the bicycle, all meadow flowers, hills, trees and all sky/clouds outside kite/tail/string. No photographic texture, no grey, no labels, no borders. White is the area where the kite was added; black preserves original pixels.

Use case: precise-object-edit. Output ONLY a black-and-white binary removal mask accurately registered to this input photograph. Preserve exact input framing and portrait aspect ratio. Paint SOLID WHITE the complete red bicycle in the right foreground (all wheels, spokes, frame, handlebars, saddle, rack, pedals and contact shadow), AND the red-blue kite in the upper-left sky, its ribbon tail and complete fine white string descending toward the field. Add a small 4-pixel safety margin around selected edges so removals leave no remnants. Important registration: bicycle handlebars start around x617,y681, saddle at x784,y754; bicycle occupies x444..1055,y681..1030 in the 1086x1448 input. Kite spans x288..356,y175..253, with tail to x235,y316 and string to about x525,y683. Leave gaps inside bicycle frame and spokes BLACK. All other meadow, clouds, sky, hills, trees and fence must be SOLID BLACK. No photographic texture, no grey shading, no text or borders. This mask will replace those selected areas with the empty scene from the next edit.
processing: All composite RGB pixels come only from the original photograph or the five supplied edits, resized as needed and blended through masks. The string selection comes from the supplied image-tool mask and copies actual source-photo pixels. No drawn or reconstructed image content. Removals restore original pixels under the corresponding addition masks.
